references.text: Jacob promises to give a tenth back to God, in response to God's blessings, similar to how Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth.
The Mosaic law requires a tenth of the harvest, reflecting the principle of tithing that Abram practiced toward Melchizedek.
The author of Hebrews refers to Melchizedek as a type for Christ and mentions Abraham's tithe to him, illustrating a principle of recognition and honor to God.
"God – his way is perfect" – a praise of God as shield, reflecting Melchizedek's blessing of "God Most High who has given your enemies into your hand".
Psalm 110:4 speaks of a priest "forever after the order of Melchizedek," linking Melchizedek's priesthood to messianic expectation.
Hebrews confirms and interprets the event of Abraham's tithe to Melchizedek from Genesis.
Hebrews builds its theological argument directly on the event in Genesis 14.
Direct allusion to Abraham's action with the spoils of war in Genesis 14.
